candidate_evidence.quote: This is an ongoing Phase 2, open-label, single-center, non-randomized study of sintilimab (one anti-PD-1 antibody same as nivolumab approved in China) plus bevacizumab administered in a low dosage schedule

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: in adult (≥ 18 years) participants with a clinical relapse or circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-level relapse of glioblastoma (GBM).

role_evidence.quote: Both cohorts will receive the same study drug sintilimab 200mg and bevacizumab 3mg/kg every 3 weeks.
Sintilimab (One Anti-PD-1 Antibody) Plus Low-dose Bevacizumab for ctDNA-level-relapse and Clinical-relapse Glioblastoma

agents.drug_class_hint: anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody, established GBM therapy (low-dose schedule)

biomarkers.biomarker_other: tumour in situ fluid (TISF) ctDNA dynamics (ctDNA-level relapse)

source_quote.quote: Cohort 1: Subjects with ctDNA-level-relapse glioblastoma before clinical relapse, determined according to the dynamics of TISF ctDNA.
-To evaluate the correlative biomarkers based on TISF ctDNA.

coder_notes: Registered intervention name says 'Tislelizumab plus Bevacizumab' but description, title, summary and brand (TYVYT) all indicate sintilimab; coded sintilimab - adjudicator should confirm moiety. Record states sintilimab is approved in China (possible other_regulator_only for [LOOKUP]). Bevacizumab (established GBM therapy, D6) given at low dose to all participants; coded established_therapy_experiment because the low-dose schedule is part of the investigated regimen (soc_backbone also defensible; neither is a candidate). TISF ctDNA relapse determines cohort assignment (enrichment), not mechanistically linked to PD-1 blockade. Outcome text mentions 'durvalumab' (apparent copy error).
